a.xlink:title: Asks to review the run, prepares the scene, builds the canvas and starts the simulation.
Seconds since midnight of an "hh:mm:ss" base time; 0 when the text is empty or not a time of day.
The case layers panel shows the case name and the clock time.
The number of diagnostics of each severity.
The message of the first error among the diagnostics, else of the first diagnostic,...
True when a diagnostic has severity Error.
The scene is about to be prepared. The window shows that and lets the events through.
What the actions of the window enable depends on the scene or on the run, and one of them changed.
The next run writes to the folder of the scene sceneName, unless the user chose a folder.
Starts the run on a worker thread. The scene has to be prepared.
The run of the process. Its address never changes.
Stores the settings of the run and its window length. Does nothing unless enabled().
True when QEGTRAIN_PLAYBACK_PROFILE was "1" when the profiler was created.
The profiler of the process, created at the first call.
The first error among the diagnostics, else the first diagnostic, else null.
The same run with write access, for the stages of the controller and for tests. The thread rules of r...
Empties run.infra, the platforms of the run and its final-station statistics.
The reset between scene runs, which is the same as preparing a new run.
Selects the scenario with the id id.
The output folder that prepareScene applies to the next run, or empty. Call this on the GUI thread.
Execution-thread observation: runSimulation starts the run.
Execution-thread observations, independent of GUI result availability: runSimulation turns down a run...
The one set of hooks of the process: free functions read it, and main builds one MainWindow.
The editors, the infrastructure dock and the actions follow the run state.
Pause and Stop mean something while a run exists, and Output Folder only while none does.
The run starts: the window ends the replay of an earlier run and shows the progress.
A worker without a controller runs the controller of the process, the global simulation.
The worker of the run. Qt deletes it when its thread has finished; null while no run exists.
The worker is set up and its thread starts next.
A count with the noun that fits it, such as "1 error" or "2 errors".
